AXP.rationale: American Express demonstrates solid fundamental health with strong revenue and EPS growth trajectory (Q1 2026 revenue +9.3% YoY, EPS +17.6% YoY), high profitability (ROE ~33-34%, net margin ~26-27%), and a premium closed-loop business model with durable competitive advantages. The company's affluent customer base provides resilience, with cardmember spending up 10% YoY in Q1  luxury retail spending up 18%. However, the stock is trading near the low end of its 365-day P/E range (19.1x vs. 18.9-25.3x range), suggesting some valuation support after a -8.8% quarterly price decline. The recent Q1 earnings beat (EPS $4.28 vs. $4.06 consensus) and analyst upgrades (Freedom Broker to Buy, BofA PT raised to $387) provide a near-term catalyst, though the stock's reaction was muted. Risks include rising 10-year Treasury yields (4.47%), elevated oil prices ($104.66/bbl) potentially pressuring consumer spending, and macro uncertainty. The balance sheet shows rising debt ($58.75B) but manageable leverage (D/E 1.73x). Operating cash flow declined QoQ (-39%) but this appears seasonal. Overall, a quality franchise at a reasonable valuation with modest near-term upside potential.

Analyst upgrades post-earnings: Freedom Broker to Buy ($370 PT), BofA raised PT to $387
